findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Security
Case: normal use - a review has an unscored P2 advisory and another blocker; after the owner splits them, a later review finds a different P0 authorization flaw at another line of the same file with the advisory's title. `src/forge/close.py:128` splits every open finding, including advice. Because an unscored finding has no score-bar outcome, `src/forge/review.py:632` records its split reason as `known: Split into...`. This new exception then carries that settlement onto the P0, so it does not block. The earlier ruling concerned a cited dismissal or fixed finding; this new split-advisory path defeats the coordinator's explicit requirement that old advice not cover a different serious finding.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - an owner chooses Split for findings at the review limit, then closes the original item or reviews later edits. For a fix's `Not done:` finding, `src/forge/close.py:290` calls `bound_review`, which removes the split follow-up at `src/forge/review.py:1095` and makes the saved finding block again. Separately, if an earlier advisory had the same file and title as a later serious finding, `_settled` uses `setdefault` at `src/forge/review.py:632`, so the earlier below-bar reason wins over the later owner's split; a subsequent review reopens that serious finding. The new exception never sees a split reason in either case. The named split test uses fresh, ordinary P1 findings and does not expose these paths.
